newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: LAW APPROVED FOR SALE OF 26 PCT PORTUGAL TELECOM.
newsitem.headline: LAW APPROVED FOR SALE OF 26 PCT PORTUGAL TELECOM.

text.p: The Portuguese cabinet approved a law authorising the sale of a further 26 percent of the capital of Portugal Telecom, the country's dominant telecommunications operator, in a third stage privatisation, a spokesman said.

The sale, due in the final quarter of 1997, will include a public offer to sell (OPV) on the domestic market and two direct sales, one of which will be to strategic partners, the spokesman told reporters.
One of the two direct sales will be to domestic and foreign financial institutions.
The other will be to strategic partners, which must be telecommunications operators, at the same price as the direct sale to the institutions.
The division of the stakes to be sold among the total 49 million shares for sale in the third stage privatisation will be decided later, the spokesman said.
The privatisation price will be fixed later by a resolution of the cabinet.
The Portuguese government has so far sold off 49 percent of the capital of PT in two previous privatisations.
Portugal Telecom shares were trading at 7,545 escudos, up 95, in volume of 220,437 shares on Lisbon bourse at 1503 GMT.
The OPV will include a tranche reserved for employees, small shareholders and emigrants, as well as PT bondholders.

In the tranche reserved for domestic and foreign institutions, an increase in supply of up to 10 percent of the shares in the direct sale could be made available if demand is strong, the cabinet spokesman said.
Later, PT shares edged higher to 7,570 escudos, a high for the session, up 120 in volume of 227,547 shares at 1517 GMT.
